positions.title: Software Engineer II
positions.description:
•	Design, develop, and maintain scalable C++ software solutions in the airline commerce space, leading feature development (e.g., availability calculator) and collaborating with cross-functional teams and clients to align technical implementation with user needs and business goals.
•	Bridge business needs and technical execution by collaborating with stakeholders to improve and develop new documentation, roadmaps, and process workflows that guide configuration, testing, and deployment of scalable applications.
•	Participate in team code reviews, ensuring adherence to best practices and enhancing code quality across the team.
•	Execute comprehensive testing strategies, including regression, load, and unit testing, modify test scripts for troubleshooting, and maintain logs to monitor and improve application performance.
•	Drive agile development by reporting project status, managing task priorities in JIRA, contributing to Scrum ceremonies (stand-ups, sprint planning, retrospectives), and maintaining clear team documentation in Confluence to support alignment and transparency.

positions.title: Research Assistant
positions.description:
•	Conduct interdisciplinary research in the LEARN-CS Lab, collaborating with faculty and students on projects exploring equity and alternative pathways in computer science education.
•	Designed and led a full-cycle custom research study—from initial problem framing through photovoice sessions and in-depth group interviews to investigate how students navigate computing programs and identify behavioral and attitudinal drivers of persistence.
•	Designed and implemented an interview protocol to conduct in-depth qualitative interviews, ensuring data collection aligned with ethical research standards and addressed key research questions.
•	Developed and administered surveys to gather both qualitative and quantitative data; conducted statistical analysis in R to identify key trends.
•	Co-coordinated a Research Experience for Undergraduates (REU) program at The Ohio State University, mentoring undergraduate students, guiding them in research methodology, and fostering a collaborative research environment.
•	Presented findings at national conferences (e.g., ASEE, FIE) and contributed to journal publications on computing education.
•	Selected to attend the 2025 SEFI PhD Summer School in the Netherlands, where I engaged with international researchers on qualitative methods and academic publishing practices.

positions.title: Learning Assistant
positions.description:
•	Served as classroom facilitator to ease transition to active learning for underclassmen. Assisted students in enhancing their computer applications through thorough trouble shooting and critical analysis of their work.
•	Provided additional assistance to students through office hours to help students dissect course material, develop a deeper understanding of computer structures, and apply their new knowledge to improve their final project outcomes.

positions.title: Content Contributor
positions.description:
•	Designed and authored interactive articles, lessons, quizzes, and coding projects across multiple course tracks (Fundamentals of Operating Systems, Intermediate Java, Advanced Java), ensuring pedagogical clarity and alignment with intended learning outcomes. 
•	Collaborated closely with the Curriculum team to define educational objectives, coordinate development timelines, and deliver an engaging learner experience.

positions.title: Capital Markets Technology Intern
positions.description:
Participated in the design, development, integration, testing, deployment, and support of technology solutions for Asset Back Finance department, specifically in the replacement of a legacy application used to monitor pricing, risk, profit and loss for business functions.
Developed and maintained desktop applications programmed using Java with Spring Framework, and C# with .NET.

organizations.name: Upsilon Pi Epsilon Honor Society
organizations.description: Upsilon Pi Epsilon (UPE) is the first and only international honor society for the computing and information disciplines. Florida International University is home to the award-winning Mu Chapter of Florida - the premier student organization at FIU's School of Computing and Information Sciences. It consists of the largest and most active group of students majoring in the computing and information disciplines. UPE provides a large number of benefits and rewards to its members, and hosts a wide range of activities such as info sessions, technical workshops, and social events.
